definition_en: what can be seen from a place, or the way a person thinks about something
core_image: 推开旅馆的窗，整片湖面铺在眼前
scene: 旅馆房间在六楼，她拉开窗帘，整片湖面就铺在眼前。 The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 view 是「景色」（第 1 个义项：从某处能看到的景象）；句意为这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。推开窗后铺开的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「观众；观看者」
合成词，义为「观点；视角」
加前缀 re- 构成，义为「回顾；评论」

senses.title: What can be seen from a place
senses.definition: the whole scene that a place allows you to see
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置能看到的整体景象
senses.example: The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。
senses.why: To look out is to see; the scene laid before the eyes is the view.
senses.whyCN: 向外看是「看」这个动作，而铺在眼前的那片景象就是 view。

senses.title: A person’s opinion about something
senses.definition: a particular way of thinking about a matter
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的特定想法
senses.example: In my view the plan costs too much.
senses.exampleCN: 在我看来这个计划花费太高。
senses.why: The eye and the mind use one word: what you see from where you stand is what you think from where you stand.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛与头脑共用一个词：从哪个位置看，就从哪个位置想。

senses.title: The range within which something can be seen
senses.definition: the area that can be seen from a point, or the chance to see something
senses.definitionCN: 从一个位置能看见的区域，或看见某物的机会
senses.example: The ship came into view at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时那艘船出现在视野里。
senses.why: A view is not only the picture but the space in which the picture can appear.
senses.whyCN: view 不只是那幅画面，也是画面得以出现的空间。

senses.title: To look at something carefully
senses.definition: to watch or examine something, especially for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有目的地观看或检查某物
senses.example: The committee viewed the site before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在表决前察看了现场。
senses.why: The noun gives a verb: to give a thing your view is to view it.
senses.whyCN: 名词派生动词：把目光给某物，就是去观看它。

senses.title: To regard something in a certain way
senses.definition: to think of something as being a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物视为某一性质的事物
senses.example: Many people view silence as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 很多人把沉默看作同意。
senses.why: When the mind places a thing before itself, the same verb names the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 当头脑把一物摆在自身之前端详时，这个动词也用来表示判断。

senses.title: What can be seen in a picture or on a screen
senses.definition: the scene shown in an image, drawing, or display
senses.definitionCN: 图像、图画或屏幕中显示的场景
senses.example: The drawing shows the house from the front view.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画从正面视角画了这座房子。
senses.why: Images repeat the word, naming the angle from which a scene is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 图像沿用了这个词，用来指画面取景的角度。

intro.en: View comes from Old French veue, a seeing, from Latin videre, to see.
intro.cn: view 来自古法语 veue（看见），源头是拉丁语 videre（看）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visus gave the noun of seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其过去分词 visus 派生出「所见」的名词。

items.en: French veue named the act of seeing and the sight itself.
items.cn: 法语 veue 既指看的动作，也指所见之物。

items.en: English borrowed it as vewe, later spelled view.
items.cn: 英语借入作 vewe，后来拼作 view。

items.en: The sense widened from sight to the scene before the eyes.
items.cn: 词义从「看」扩展到眼前的景象。

items.en: Opinion and examination joined the family, giving in my view and to view a site.
items.cn: 「看法」与「检查」加入词族，产生 in my view 与 view a site。

note.en: The first group holds words built on view, the second the words for scenes and opinions.
note.cn: 第一组是由 view 构成的词，第二组是表示景象与看法的词。

normalIntro.en: Latin to see becomes both the thing seen and the thought held: the eye and the mind share one short word.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「看」既成为所见之物，也成为所持之见：眼睛与头脑共用一个短词。

normal.en: View is short but the vowel is long: /vjuː/.
normal.cn: view 拼写不长，但元音读长音 /vjuː/。

normal.en: Viewer adds -er for the one watching.
normal.cn: viewer 加 -er 表示观看的人。

normal.en: Viewpoint joins view and point, a place to think from.
normal.cn: viewpoint 由 view 与 point 合成，指思考所站的位置。

normal.en: Review begins with re-, to look again.

normal.en: In my view is the standard way to give an opinion.

abstract.en: Hear someone say that is how I see it.

examples.cn: 从塔顶望去，整座小镇尽收眼底。

examples.en: The council viewed the plans with suspicion.
examples.cn: 议会带着怀疑看待这些计划。

examples.en: Her view of the matter changed after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议之后，她对这件事的看法变了。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ 过去分词 visus → 古法语 veue → 英语 view

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a scene from a window and ends with a judgment in the mind; the verb bridges watching and regarding.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从窗外的景象开始，走到心中的判断；动词则连接了「观看」与「看作」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lake spread out beyond an open window.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞开的窗外铺开一片湖。

branches.en: The window branch: lake and hills from a room.
branches.cn: 窗户分支：房里望见的湖与山。

branches.en: The opinion branch: my view on the cost.

branches.en: The range branch: a ship heaving into sight.

branches.en: The drawing branch: a house shown from the front view.
branches.cn: 绘图分支：房子的正面视图。

intro.en: The root vid-, vis-, view- means to see; -er, -point, and re- extend the word.
intro.cn: 词根 vid-、vis-、view- 意为看见，-er、-point、re- 扩展这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, passed through French as veue and reaches English as view, with its relatives visible and vision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）经法语 veue 传入英语成为 view，同族还有 visible 与 vision。

definition_en: foolish or not sensible, often in a harmless way
core_image: 一个人把纸帽扣在头上，自己先笑出声
scene: 别问这么傻的问题。 Don't ask such a silly question.
sceneCN: 这里 silly 是「愚蠢的、傻的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：别问这么傻的问题。

derivatives.zh: 愚蠢；傻气
愚蠢地

senses.title: Foolish
senses.definition: showing a lack of good sense
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏判断力的
senses.example: Don't ask such a silly question.
senses.exampleCN: 别问这么傻的问题。
senses.why: This is the basic foolish sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的愚蠢义项。

senses.title: Funny or absurd
senses.definition: funny or strange in a light way
senses.definitionCN: 轻松意义上的滑稽或古怪
senses.example: He made a silly face.
senses.exampleCN: 他做了个鬼脸。
senses.why: Foolishness can also be playful.
senses.whyCN: 愚蠢也可以是玩闹的。

intro.en: Silly once meant happy and blessed.
intro.cn: silly 最初意为幸福的、有福的。

items.en: Saelig meant happy or blessed.
items.cn: saelig 意为幸福的、有福的。

items.en: The word meant innocent or simple.
items.cn: 这个词意为天真或单纯的。

items.en: The form became silly.
items.cn: 词形演变为 silly。

items.en: The sense shifted to foolish.
items.cn: 词义转向愚蠢的。

items.en: It also described playful humor.
items.cn: 它也用来形容玩闹式的幽默。

note.en: Silly is compared with similar-looking words and with words for foolishness.
note.cn: 把 silly 与形近词以及表示愚蠢的词作比较。

entries.definition: a fine soft cloth

unwise

normalIntro.en: Silly is foolishness with a smile.
normalIntro.cn: silly 是带着笑意的愚蠢。

normal.en: They shared a silly joke.

abstract.en: Silly is the shadow that play casts.
abstract.cn: 傻气是玩耍投下的影子。

abstract.en: A foolish step can still make us laugh.
abstract.cn: 愚蠢的一步也能让我们发笑。

abstract.en: Children teach adults how to be silly.
abstract.cn: 孩子教大人如何犯傻。

examples.en: I made a silly mistake.

dict_mnemonic.text: silly 最初是「有福的」，后来变成「单纯的」，再变成「傻的」；记住它可以带着笑。

root: 源自古英语 sælig（有福的），词义经「天真的」演变为「愚蠢的」，核心义「缺乏判断力」。

sensesIntro.en: Silly means foolish or funny in a light way.
sensesIntro.cn: silly 意为愚蠢的或轻松可笑的。

core.en: Sense taking a holiday.

definition_zh: 干的；干燥的；干旱的；干渴的；弄干；变干；枯燥的
definition_en: free from water or liquid, or to remove water from something
core_image: 湿衣服在阳光下一点点收干
scene: 雨停后的庭院里，晾衣绳上的衬衫被太阳晒得半干。 Hang the shirt outside so the sun can dry it.
sceneCN: 这里 dry 是动词「弄干、晒干」（第 4 个义项：去除水分）；句意：把衬衫挂到外面让太阳晒干它。

pos.zh: 干的；干旱的；干渴的；枯燥的

derivatives.zh: dry 加表示物的后缀 er 构成，义为「干燥剂；烘干机」
dry 加 ness 构成，义为「干燥；干渴」
dry 加 er 构成，义为「烘干机」

senses.title: Free from water
senses.definition: without water or liquid inside or on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 内部或表面没有水或液体
senses.example: The towel was dry after a night on the line.
senses.exampleCN: 晾了一夜后毛巾干透了。
senses.why: The base picture is a cloth with no wetness left.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的画面是一块不再湿的布。

senses.title: With little rain
senses.definition: having little rain or a low level of moisture
senses.definitionCN: 降雨很少或湿度很低
senses.example: The dry season lasts from October to March.
senses.exampleCN: 旱季从十月持续到三月。
senses.why: A place without water is dry the way a towel without water is dry.
senses.whyCN: 缺水的地方与缺水的毛巾一样「干」。

senses.title: Thirsty
senses.definition: feeling the need to drink
senses.definitionCN: 感到需要喝水
senses.example: After the long run, my throat felt dry.
senses.exampleCN: 长跑之后我觉得喉咙发干。
senses.why: A dry mouth reminds the body it needs water.
senses.whyCN: 发干的口腔提醒身体需要水分。

senses.title: Remove water
senses.definition: to take the water out of something, or to lose water
senses.definitionCN: 除去某物中的水分，或失去水分
senses.example: Dry your hands with this towel.
senses.exampleCN: 用这条毛巾把手擦干。
senses.why: The state of having no water becomes the act of reaching that state.
senses.whyCN: 「没有水」的状态引申为达到该状态的动作。

senses.title: Boring and plain
senses.definition: not interesting because it has no colour or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味、色彩或感情
senses.example: The report was dry but full of facts.
senses.exampleCN: 报告枯燥，但资料翔实。
senses.why: A subject without juice or feeling feels like dry bread.
senses.whyCN: 没有汁水与感情的题目，尝起来像干面包。

senses.title: Understated humour
senses.definition: funny in a quiet, seemingly serious way
senses.definitionCN: 以平静、看似严肃的方式逗人发笑
senses.example: She told the joke with dry humour.
senses.exampleCN: 她面无表情地讲了这个笑话。
senses.why: No laughing water on the face: the joke stays bone-dry.
senses.whyCN: 脸上不带笑意的「水分」，笑话保持十足干燥。

intro.en: Dry is a plain Germanic word about the absence of water, old enough to have no clear relatives outside the family.
intro.cn: dry 是一个朴素的日耳曼词，核心是「缺水」，古老得在词族之外找不到清晰亲戚。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *draugiz meant dry, related to words for dried wood.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *draugiz 意为干燥的，与指干木的词相关。

items.en: Old English drȳge meant dry, free from moisture.
items.cn: 古英语 drȳge 意为干燥的、无水分的。

items.en: Old Norse drygr may have influenced the Middle English vowel.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 drygr 可能影响了中古英语的元音。

items.en: Middle English dri extended to drought, thirst and plain talk.
items.cn: 中古英语 dri 扩展到干旱、口渴与平淡话语。

items.en: Modern English settled the verb to dry and the dry humour of quiet comedy.
items.cn: 现代英语定型了动词 to dry，以及冷面幽默的用法。

note.en: These words stand near dry in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 dry 相邻。

definition_en: at the present time, especially when the present is set against the past
core_image: 一张旧照片和一张新照片并排摆着，同一条街已经换了模样
scene: 老人在巷口翻出旧相片，指着同一处街角说当年的店铺早就不在了。 Nowadays the street is full of coffee shops instead of grocery stores.
sceneCN: 这里是「现今、如今」（第 1 个义项：指当下的时间）；句意为如今这条街上全是咖啡馆，不再是杂货店。旧照与新街并置，让这个词的时间感更清楚。

derivatives.zh: 由 now 与 day 缩合而来的形容词，多见于旧用法，义为「现今的」
nowadays 的构词基干之一，源自古英语 nu，义为「现在」

senses.title: At the present time
senses.definition: at the present time, in the period we are living in now
senses.definitionCN: 在我们正生活的当下这个时期
senses.example: Nowadays most people carry a phone everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 如今大多数人走到哪里都带着手机。
senses.why: The phrase behind the word literally meant now on days, so its first job is simply to place an action in the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的短语字面上就是「如今在这些日子里」，所以它最基本的工作是把动作安放在当下。

senses.title: The present seen against the past
senses.definition: used to point out how things differ between the present and an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出现在与从前之间的差别
senses.example: Nowadays we order food online, but my grandmother still walks to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 如今我们在网上点菜，可我祖母还是走去菜市场。
senses.why: Because the phrase grew out of a comparison between days, the word naturally carries a before-and-after frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语本就诞生于「日子与日子」的对照，所以这个词天然带着「前后之别」的框架。

senses.title: Of the present period, placed before a noun
senses.titleCN: 时下的；当今的（口语用法）
senses.definition: placed before a noun in informal speech to mean belonging to the present period
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在名词前，表示属于当下这个时期的
senses.example: Nowadays children learn to swipe a screen before they learn to write.
senses.exampleCN: 现在的孩子先学会滑屏幕，再学会写字。
senses.why: Once the adverb is felt as a label for the current era, speakers begin to use it as a modifier of the people and things that belong to that era.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词被当成「当下时代」的标签，说话人就开始把它放到名词前，修饰属于这个时代的人与物。

intro.en: Nowadays began as a spoken phrase rather than a single word: now on days, which English later squeezed into one adverb.
intro.cn: nowadays 起初是一个口语短语而不是单词：now on days，后来英语把它压缩成一个副词。

items.en: The two halves are old: nu meant now, and dæg meant day.
items.cn: 两半都很古老：nu 意为「现在」，dæg 意为「日子」。

items.en: Middle English joined them in the phrase now a dayes, literally now on days, with a as a worn-down form of on.
items.cn: 中古英语把它们连成 now a dayes，字面是「如今在这些日子里」，其中的 a 是 on 的弱化形式。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the phrase was written as one word, and the old preposition had disappeared from hearing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个短语被写成一个词，旧的介词在听感上已经消失。

items.en: Dictionaries of the eighteenth century list it as a settled adverb of present time.
items.cn: 十八世纪的词典已把它收作表示现在时间的固定副词。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly in writing and in contrastive statements about how things have changed.
items.cn: 现代英语主要在书面语里、以及在说明事物如何变化的今昔对比句中使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short time words built from the same demonstrative parts; the near-meaning group collects other ways of saying now.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一批指示词构成的短小时间词，近义组收其他表示「现在」的说法。

normalIntro.en: Split the word into now, a and dayes and it says now on these days, which is simply the present.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 now、a、dayes 三段，意思就是「在这些日子里」，也就是现在。

normal.en: Nowadays hides the words now and day inside it, and together they mean now on these days.
normal.cn: nowadays 里藏着 now 与 day，合起来就是「如今在这些日子里」。

normal.en: The a in the middle is a worn-down on, so the phrase once read as now on days.
normal.cn: 中间那个 a 是弱化掉的 on，所以这个短语原本读作 now on days。

normal.en: The final -s is the plural of day, which is why the word points to a stretch of days rather than one date.
normal.cn: 末尾的 -s 是 day 的复数，所以这个词指的是一段日子，而不是某一天。

normal.en: Nowadays is an adverb, so in careful writing it modifies a whole clause rather than standing before a noun.
normal.cn: nowadays 是副词，在严谨的写作里它修饰整个句子，而不是站在名词前面。

normal.en: Its closest short synonym in speech is these days, which carries the same contrast with the past.
normal.cn: 口语里它最贴近的短说法是 these days，同样带着与过去对照的意味。

abstract.en: The word is a fossil of a phrase: a whole remark about days was squeezed until it fit into one slot.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个短语的化石：一句关于日子的话被压缩到只占一个位置。

abstract.en: Hearing nowadays always implies a before, because a contrast with the past is built into its bones.
abstract.cn: 听到 nowadays 总会预设一个「从前」，因为与过去的对照已经长在它的骨架里。

abstract.en: It measures time the way a photograph does: it does not give the clock, only the fact that the picture has changed.
abstract.cn: 它衡量时间的方式像一张照片：它不报钟点，只说明画面已经变了。

intro.en: Central comes from Latin centrum, the sharp point of a compass.
intro.cn: central 来自拉丁语 centrum，指圆规的固定尖端。

items.en: Greek kentron means a sharp point, especially the needle of a drawing compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 意为「尖点」，尤指画圆用圆规的针尖。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as centrum, the fixed point around which a circle is drawn.
items.cn: 拉丁语将其借为 centrum，即画圆时固定的中心点。

items.en: Medieval writers used centralis for things at the centre.
items.cn: 中世纪学者用 centralis 表示「处于中心的」。

items.en: French formed central, and English took the word in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语形成 central，英语于十七世纪借入。

items.en: Later it widened from place to importance: a central idea, a central role.
items.cn: 后来它从位置扩展到重要性：中心思想、核心作用。

senses.title: Having the power to act
senses.definition: having the power or chance to do something

senses.example: She is able to swim across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 她能够游过这条河。

senses.title: Freedom from outside control
senses.definition: the state of being free from control by another person, group or country

senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱而不必依赖他人

senses.why: The cut is remembered as a feast.
senses.whyCN: 那次剪断被当作节日纪念。

intro.en: Independence is depend with in- (not) and the noun ending -ence. Depend itself comes from Latin de- (down) + pendere (to hang): to hang from something.
intro.cn: independence 由 depend 加否定前缀 in- 与名词后缀 -ence 构成。depend 出自拉丁语 de-「向下」+ pendere「悬挂」，本义是「挂在某物上」。

items.en: Latin pendere meant to hang; scales hung and weighed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂；天平悬起称量。

items.en: de- plus pendere formed dependere: to hang down from.
items.cn: de- 加 pendere 构成 dependere：从……垂挂下来。

items.en: Old French dependre carried the idea of hanging upon.
items.cn: 古法语 dependre 保留「悬挂于上」之意。

items.en: Middle English dependen meant to hang down, then to rely on.
items.cn: 中古英语 dependen 先指垂下，后指依赖。

items.en: English added in- and -ence to name the state of not hanging on anyone.
items.cn: 英语加上 in- 与 -ence，命名不依附任何人的状态。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the hang-root family. The meaning group compares words of standing free.
note.cn: 形近组收录「悬挂」词根词族；词义组比较表示独立自主的词。

entries.definition: the adjective of the same family.
the state of relying on others.
to hang up, from the same pendere.
the general power to act as one wishes.
entries.definitionCN: 按自己意愿行动的普遍能力。

entries.definition: self-rule of a group or person.
trusting your own efforts.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the hanging root, the cut-strings image and the holiday name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「悬挂」词根、剪线意象与节日名称。

normal.en: de-pend: hang down; in-dependence: not hanging on anyone.
normal.cn: depend 是垂挂；independence 是不挂在任何人身上。

normal.en: Independence Day is the national birthday.
normal.cn: 独立日是国家的生日。

normal.en: gain independence is the standard phrase for new countries.
normal.cn: gain independence 是新国家获得独立的固定说法。

normal.en: declare independence echoes the famous declaration.
normal.cn: declare independence 呼应著名的《独立宣言》。

normal.en: dependence is the twin that still hangs.
normal.cn: dependence 是还在垂挂的孪生词。

abstract.en: One image: a puppet whose strings fall cut to the floor.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：木偶的提线齐齐断落在地。

abstract.en: Independence is the moment you stop borrowing legs.
abstract.cn: 独立是不再借腿走路的那一刻。

abstract.en: A country standing on its own feet, like a person.
abstract.cn: 国家像人一样自己站稳。

examples.en: India gained independence in nineteen forty-seven.
examples.cn: 印度于一九四七年获得独立。

examples.en: She values her independence above everything.
examples.cn: 她把独立看得高于一切。

examples.en: The village declared its independence from the old system.
examples.cn: 村庄宣布脱离旧体制而独立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因迪潘登斯」：不再「等」着别人「攀登」，自己站起来， independence。

root: 拉丁语 de-「向下」+ pendere「悬挂」→ dependere「垂挂」→ 古法语/中古英语 depend「依赖」→ 加否定前缀 in- 与名词后缀 -ence 得 independence「不依赖的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Independence is the cut string: a nation free from a ruler, a person free to decide, a wallet free of debt, and the holiday that remembers the cut.
sensesIntro.cn: independence 是剪断的线：国家摆脱统治者、个人自己做主、钱包不再欠债，以及纪念那一剪的节日。

core.en: Cut strings: standing without being hung or pulled by anyone.
core.cn: 剪断的提线：不被任何人悬挂或牵引地站立。

branches.en: NATIONHOOD: the colony won independence.
branches.cn: 国家层面：殖民地赢得独立。

branches.en: SELFHOOD: living alone taught her independence.
branches.cn: 个人层面：独居教会她自立。

branches.en: MONEY: financial independence from a job.
branches.cn: 经济层面：兼职带来经济独立。

branches.en: MEMORY: fireworks on Independence Day.
branches.cn: 纪念：独立日的烟花。

branches.en: STANDING: free to act without pull.
branches.cn: 自立：不受牵引地行动。

intro.en: Independence builds its adjective independent and the opposite dependence.
intro.cn: independence 派生出形容词 independent 及反义名词 dependence。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the hanging verb pendere behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的悬挂动词 pendere。

definition_en: in a sad way; in a way that shows regret; unfortunately
core_image: 低声说话、缓缓摇头的悲伤神情
scene: 她悲伤地摇了摇头。 She shook her head sadly.
sceneCN: 这里 sadly 是「悲伤地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她悲伤地摇了摇头。

derivatives.zh: 悲伤的；难过的
悲伤；难过
使悲伤；使难过

senses.title: In a sad way
senses.definition: with feelings of sorrow or unhappiness
senses.definitionCN: 带着悲伤或不快的情绪
senses.example: She looked sadly at the old photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 她悲伤地看着那张旧照片。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the feeling into a manner.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把情绪转成做事的方式。

senses.title: With regret
senses.definition: with a feeling of disappointment or regret
senses.definitionCN: 带着失望或遗憾的心情
senses.example: Sadly, the train had already left.
senses.exampleCN: 遗憾的是，火车已经开走了。
senses.why: Regret colors the speaker's comment on a fact.
senses.whyCN: 遗憾给说话人对事实的评论染上色彩。

senses.title: Unfortunately
senses.definition: used to say that something is unfortunate
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事不幸或令人惋惜
senses.example: Sadly, many families lost their homes.
senses.exampleCN: 不幸的是，许多家庭失去了家园。
senses.why: The sentence adverb marks bad news.
senses.whyCN: 句子副词用来标记坏消息。

intro.en: Sadly is sad plus the adverb ending -ly, from Old English -lice.
intro.cn: sadly 由 sad 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，-ly 源自古英语 -lice。

items.en: The ending -lice forms adverbs of manner.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 构成方式副词。

items.en: The ending becomes -ly in everyday use.
items.cn: 中古英语中该词尾在日常使用中变为 -ly。

items.en: Sadly describes how someone speaks or moves.
items.cn: sadly 描述某人说话或动作的方式。

items.en: Sadly also comments on unfortunate facts.
items.cn: sadly 也可评述不幸的事实。

items.en: The pattern is adjective plus -ly.
items.cn: 构词模式是形容词加 -ly。

note.en: Sadly means with sorrow; badly means in a poor way.
note.cn: sadly 是悲伤地，badly 则是糟糕地。

entries.definition: in a poor or harmful way
in a wild or very eager way
with pleasure
in an unhappy way
with a feeling of regret
by bad luck or in a sad way

normalIntro.en: Sadly tells how something is done or comments on bad news.
normalIntro.cn: sadly 既说明事情如何发生，也可用来评论坏消息。

normal.en: She smiled sadly and closed the door.
normal.cn: 她悲伤地笑了笑，关上了门。

normal.en: He spoke sadly about his old school.
normal.cn: 他悲伤地谈起自己的母校。

normal.en: Sadly, the concert was cancelled.
normal.cn: 遗憾的是，音乐会被取消了。

normal.en: The dog waited sadly by the gate.
normal.cn: 狗悲伤地在门边等候。

normal.en: Sadly, few people came to the meeting.
normal.cn: 不幸的是，来开会的人很少。

abstract.en: Picture a person speaking in a low, slow voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人用低沉缓慢的声音说话。

abstract.en: Imagine a head shaking slowly from side to side.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗头缓缓地左右摇动。

abstract.en: Think of a sigh that comes before bad news.
abstract.cn: 想象坏消息到来前的一声叹息。

examples.en: She looked sadly at the empty chair.
examples.cn: 她悲伤地看着那把空椅子。

examples.en: Sadly, the museum closed last year.
examples.cn: 遗憾的是，博物馆去年关闭了。

examples.en: He smiled sadly and said goodbye.
examples.cn: 他悲伤地微笑着道别。

dict_mnemonic.text: sad 加副词后缀 -ly，表示「以悲伤的方式」，就是 sadly。

root: 由形容词 sad 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，核心义「以悲伤或遗憾的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Sadly means in a sorrowful manner, with regret, or unfortunately.
sensesIntro.cn: sadly 意为以悲伤的方式、带着遗憾，或不幸地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sorrowful voice and a slow shake of the head.
core.cn: 核心意象：悲伤的嗓音与缓慢的摇头。

branches.en: The base sense is the manner of sorrow.
branches.cn: 基础义是带悲伤的行为方式。

branches.en: Disappointment adds a tone of regret.
branches.cn: 失望为语气添上遗憾。

branches.en: The adverb comments on an unfortunate fact.
branches.cn: 副词用来评述不幸的事实。

branches.en: Sorrowful manner and regretful tone overlap.
branches.cn: 悲伤的方式与遗憾的语气相互重叠。

branches.en: Regret and bad news often appear together.
branches.cn: 遗憾与坏消息常常同时出现。

intro.en: Sadly is built from sad plus the native English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: sadly 由 sad 加英语本族副词词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Sadly has no Latin root; its ending descends from Old English -lice.
latinIntro.cn: sadly 没有拉丁词根，其词尾来自古英语 -lice。

items.example: Her sadness was easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 她的悲伤很容易看出来。
这个故事让孩子们很悲伤。
那个眼神悲伤的女孩独自等候。

items.example: A sad-faced officer read the letter.
items.exampleCN: 一位面带悲伤的官员读了那封信。

definition_en: to or on a lower floor of a building
core_image: 扶着楼梯扶手往下走的脚步声
scene: 清晨七点，煎蛋的香味顺着楼梯飘进卧室。 Mum is waiting downstairs for breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 downstairs 是「在楼下」（第 1 个义项：处于楼下的低层）；句意：妈妈在楼下等早餐。

derivatives.zh: up 加 stairs 构成，义为「在楼上」，与 downstairs 相对
stair 加 case 构成，义为「楼梯（整体）」

senses.title: On or to a lower floor
senses.definition: on, or moving to, a lower floor of a building
senses.definitionCN: 在楼房低层或移向低层
senses.example: The twins raced downstairs for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 双胞胎跑下楼吃早饭。
senses.why: The word is simply down plus stairs: the steps carry you from the high floor to the low one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 down 加 stairs：台阶把你从高层送到低层。

senses.title: The lower floor as a place
senses.definition: the lower floor or rooms of a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑的低层或低层房间
senses.example: The downstairs is being painted this week.
senses.exampleCN: 本周楼下区域在刷漆。
senses.why: The direction word becomes the name of the place it points to.
senses.whyCN: 方向词变成了它所指的那个地方的名字。

intro.en: Downstairs is a plain compound: down the stairs, to the lower floor.
intro.cn: downstairs 是个朴素的复合词：顺着楼梯向下，到低层去。

items.en: Old English adun meant off the hill and staeger meant steps.
items.cn: 古英语 adun 意为下山，staeger 意为台阶。

items.en: Stair settled as the everyday word for a step or flight.
items.cn: 中古英语 stair 定型为台阶或楼梯的日常用词。

items.en: Speakers joined down and stairs into one adverb.
items.cn: 使用者把 down 与 stairs 合成一个副词。

items.en: Upstairs formed the same way as its opposite.
items.cn: upstairs 以同样的方式构成，成为它的反义词。

items.en: The word now works as adverb, adjective and noun.
items.cn: 如今它可作副词、形容词与名词。

note.en: These words sit near downstairs in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 downstairs 相邻。

entries.definition: on a higher floor
a full flight of stairs
lower along a river
entries.definitionCN: 下游（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in a lower place
a room below ground
the floor at ground level

normalIntro.en: Use the stairs picture and the pair downstairs-upstairs.
normalIntro.cn: 用「楼梯」画面和 downstairs-upstairs 这对词来记。

normal.en: go downstairs is said at the top of the steps.
normal.cn: go downstairs 是站在楼梯顶端说的话。

normal.en: downstairs is down plus stairs, easy to split.
normal.cn: downstairs 就是 down 加 stairs，一拆就懂。

normal.en: upstairs is its mirror word.
normal.cn: upstairs 是它的镜像词。

normal.en: The downstairs room often holds the kitchen.
normal.cn: 楼下的房间常是厨房。

normal.en: Breakfast smells drift downstairs in the morning.
normal.cn: 早晨的饭香会飘到楼下。

abstract.en: Feel each step soft under your socks.
abstract.cn: 感受袜子踩过每一级台阶的松软。

abstract.en: Hear your hand sliding along the rail.
abstract.cn: 听手掌滑过扶手的轻响。

abstract.en: See the warm light at the bottom of the flight.
abstract.cn: 看楼梯底端那团暖光。

examples.en: Grandma sleeps downstairs where it is warmer.
examples.cn: 奶奶睡在楼下，那里更暖和。

examples.en: The phone rang, and Dad hurried downstairs.
examples.cn: 电话响了，爸爸赶紧下楼。

examples.en: Our school library is on the downstairs floor.
examples.cn: 我们学校的图书馆在楼下那层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「当思特尔斯」——下楼时「当心」台阶「斯特尔斯」地滑

root: 复合词，由 down（向下，源自古英语 adun「下山」）加 stairs（楼梯，源自古英语 staeger「台阶」）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Downstairs is simply going down the stairs, and by extension the lower floor itself.
sensesIntro.cn: downstairs 就是顺楼梯而下，引申指楼下那层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps creaking underfoot on the way down
core.cn: 核心意象：扶着楼梯扶手往下走的脚步声

branches.en: The trip to the lower floor
branches.cn: 到低层去的那段路

branches.en: The lower rooms themselves
branches.cn: 低层的房间本身

branches.en: The creak of the third step
branches.cn: 第三级台阶的吱呀声

branches.en: Kitchen smells drifting up
branches.cn: 飘上来的厨房香气

branches.en: From going down to living down
branches.cn: 从下楼到住在楼下

intro.en: Downstairs lives with its house-word neighbours.
intro.cn: downstairs 与它的「房子词」邻居们住在一起。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Germanic: down plus stairs.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分是日耳曼语的：down 加 stairs。

definition_en: to touch someone or something with the lips, or to touch something lightly, as a ball brushing the rim
core_image: 一个人俯身，用嘴唇轻轻贴上另一个人的脸颊
scene: 车站的月台上，母亲蹲下来与远行的女儿道别。 She gave her daughter a quick kiss on the cheek before the train doors closed.
sceneCN: 这里 kiss 是「吻、亲吻」（第 1 个义项：用嘴唇接触表示亲爱或问候），句意是车门关上之前她在女儿脸颊上匆匆一吻。画面里有车站月台、母亲与女儿。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「接吻、亲吻」
由动词加 -er 构成，口语中指「亲吻的人」，也指嘴
加 -able 构成，义为「值得一吻的、可爱亲人的」
合成说法，义为「披露私情的」

senses.title: To touch with the lips
senses.definition: to touch a person or thing with the lips as a sign of love, greeting, or respect
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇触碰人或物以表示爱意、问候或敬意
senses.example: He kissed his mother on the forehead before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他离开前吻了母亲的额头。
senses.why: The core act is a small, soft touch of the lips, the most intimate gesture of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是嘴唇一次轻而柔的触碰，是嘴部最亲密的动作。

senses.title: The act or sound of kissing
senses.definition: an act of touching someone with the lips, or the sound of such a touch
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇触碰某人的行为，或这种触碰发出的声音
senses.example: She sent the children a kiss before bedtime.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们睡前她送了他们一个吻。
senses.why: The verb became a noun by naming the gesture itself, a pattern English uses again and again.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接名词化，用这个手势本身来命名，这是英语反复使用的模式。

senses.title: To touch lightly
senses.definition: to touch something very lightly, the way lips would, without pressing
senses.definitionCN: 像嘴唇那样极轻地接触某物，而不用力
senses.example: The ball kissed the top of the crossbar and went over.
senses.exampleCN: 球轻擦横梁上沿然后飞了出去。
senses.why: Because a kiss is barely a touch, the word extends to anything that grazes another surface.
senses.whyCN: 因为吻几乎算不上用力一碰，这个词便延伸到任何擦过另一表面的东西。

senses.title: To part from someone with a kiss
senses.definition: in the phrase kiss goodbye, to depart from someone with a kiss, or to give something up
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 kiss goodbye，指吻别，也指放弃某物
senses.example: You can kiss goodbye to your quiet weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以跟你安静的周末告别了。
senses.why: The farewell kiss became a compact idiom, and the second meaning treats a lost thing as something kissed away.
senses.whyCN: 告别的吻凝固成习语，第二个意思则把失去的东西当作被吻走的东西。

intro.en: Kiss is an old Germanic word, recorded in English before the Norman conquest and related to the verbs still used in German and Dutch.
intro.cn: kiss 是古老的日耳曼语词，在诺曼征服前已有英语记录，与德语、荷兰语里仍在使用的动词同源。

items.en: The verb appears as cyssan, with the noun coss, in the earliest English texts.
items.cn: 这个动词在最早的英语文本里写作 cyssan，名词为 coss。

items.en: The same root is found in German küssen and Dutch kussen, which shows a common Germanic origin.
items.cn: 同一词根见于德语 küssen 与荷兰语 kussen，说明它源自共同的日耳曼语。

items.en: Northern and eastern dialects kept short forms of the word, which fed the Middle English spelling with k.
items.cn: 北部与东部方言保留了短暂的词形，为中古英语带 k 的拼法提供了来源。

items.en: The form settle between Old and Modern English as kissen and kisse.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，词形定作 kissen 与 kisse，处在古英语与现代英语之间。

items.en: English keeps the word for the gesture and adds idioms such as kiss goodbye and kiss and make up.
items.cn: 英语保留了这个手势词，并增添了 kiss goodbye、kiss and make up 等习语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that differ from kiss by one or two letters; the near-meaning group collects other words for affection shown with the body or the lips.
note.cn: 形近组收与 kiss 相差一两个字母的词；近义组收以身体或嘴唇表达亲昵的其他词。

entries.definition: Formed directly from kiss with the suffix -able, meaning worth kissing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kiss 加 -able 直接构成，义为「值得一吻的」。

entries.definition: An old Scottish word for a chest, spelled like the past tense of kiss.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语里指「箱子」的旧词，拼法与 kiss 的过去式相同。

entries.definition: A fruit jelly once served at Russian meals, unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 曾经出现在俄式餐桌上的果冻，词源与 kiss 无关。

entries.definition: To hold someone in the arms, a bigger and more whole-bodied gesture.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人抱在怀里，动作更大、更整体。

entries.definition: A quick, light kiss, named after the bird.
entries.definitionCN: 轻快的一下亲吻，由鸟啄食的动作得名。

entries.definition: To touch someone gently with the hand, without the lips.
entries.definitionCN: 用手轻柔地抚摸，不涉及嘴唇。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic family and the set phrases in which the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的日耳曼语词族，以及这个词实际出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Kiss doubles the s before -es and -ed: kisses, kissed.
normal.cn: kiss 在加 -es 和 -ed 前要双写 s：kisses、kissed。

normal.en: German küssen and Dutch kussen keep the same root alive.
normal.cn: 德语 küssen 与荷兰语 kussen 把同一词根延续下来。

normal.en: The noun takes a modifier: a quick kiss, a goodbye kiss, a kiss on the cheek.
normal.cn: 名词常带修饰语：a quick kiss、a goodbye kiss、a kiss on the cheek。

normal.en: Blow a kiss sends the gesture through the air instead of the lips.
normal.cn: blow a kiss 是把这一手势吹出去，而不是用嘴唇贴上。

normal.en: A ball that grazes the rim is said to kiss it.
normal.cn: 擦过篮圈的球被说成对它 kiss 了一下。

abstract.en: A kiss is the smallest possible contact: two surfaces almost touching, and nothing more.
abstract.cn: 吻是可能的最轻的接触：两个表面几乎贴上，仅此而已。

abstract.en: The same word covers love and geometry; the gentleness is what the two have in common.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指爱情也指几何：两者的共同点就是那份轻。

abstract.en: To kiss something goodbye is to accept that it will not come back, as a farewell kiss marks a parting.
abstract.cn: kiss something goodbye 就是承认它不会回来，正如告别的一吻标志分离。

examples.en: She kissed her son goodnight.
examples.cn: 她吻了儿子，道一声晚安。

examples.en: The first kiss came after the film ended.
examples.cn: 电影散场后他们有了第一次亲吻。

examples.en: The shuttlecock kissed the net and dropped over.
examples.cn: 羽毛球轻擦球网后落到了对面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可斯」——轻轻可斯的一下，就是亲吻

root: 古英语 cyssan（动词）与 coss（名词），源自共同日耳曼语词根，同源于德语 küssen、荷兰语 kussen；中古英语写作 kissen、kisse，现代英语固定为 kiss，并引申出轻触与吻别义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the lips touching as a sign of love, the gesture as a noun, any very light contact, and the farewell idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：以唇触碰表示亲爱，作为名词的手势本身，任何极轻的接触，以及告别的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips resting for a moment on a cheek, the lightest touch the body makes.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇在脸颊上停留一瞬，是身体能做出的最轻的触碰。

branches.en: THE LIPS LINE: the mouth touches as a sign of love, greeting or respect.
branches.cn: 唇线：嘴部触碰，表示爱意、问候或敬意。

branches.en: THE GESTURE LINE: the touch becomes a countable thing people give and send.
branches.cn: 手势线：这份触碰变成可以送出、可以计数的一个东西。

branches.en: THE GRAZE LINE: anything that barely touches, from a ball to a breeze, borrows the word.
branches.cn: 擦碰线：从球到微风，任何几乎贴上的东西都借用这个词。

branches.en: THE PARTING LINE: the farewell kiss turns into an idiom for giving something up.
branches.cn: 离别线：告别的吻变成放弃某物的习语。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: the Germanic cousins keep the same root in German and Dutch.
branches.cn: 词族线：德语与荷兰语的同源词保留着同一词根。

intro.en: Kiss is a native Germanic word that grows mainly by inflection and by a few suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: kiss 是日耳曼本土词，主要靠词形变化以及少数后缀与合成来扩展。

latinIntro.en: Kiss has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are given only as contrasts for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: kiss 没有拉丁语祖先，下面这些拉丁词只是同一概念的对照。

items.example: The couple were kissing in the rain.
A kiss-and-tell article ruined his career.
items.exampleCN: 一篇披露私情的文章毁了他的事业。

items.example: They kissed goodbye at the gate.

definition_zh: 宫殿；王宫；主教府；豪华宅邸；大型公共文化建筑
definition_en: the official residence of a king, queen, bishop or other high dignitary, or any very large and grand building
core_image: 一道正门通向铺石大院，院后是层层抬高的殿堂，每一层都比前一层更不容外人进入
scene: 铁门后是铺石大院，台阶一层层通向正殿。 The palace opens its state rooms to visitors only two months a year.
sceneCN: 这里 palace 指「君主或高级显要的官邸」（第 1 个义项：王宫、宫殿）；句意为这座王宫每年只有两个月向访客开放国事厅。图中可辨识物件：铁门、铺石大院、台阶、正殿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 豪华大宅；大型公共建筑

derivatives.zh: 宫殿般的；宏伟的
行宫领地；普法尔茨伯爵领地
宫廷政变
宫廷革命
意大利式府邸

senses.title: The residence of a ruler
senses.definition: the official home and ceremonial centre of a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 国王、女王或皇帝的官邸与礼仪中心
senses.example: The palace balcony faces the wide avenue where crowds gather.
senses.exampleCN: 王宫的阳台朝向人群聚集的宽阔大道。
senses.why: the word began as the name of one hill in Rome, then of the emperor's house on it, and finally of any ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是罗马一座山的名字，随后指山上皇帝的宅邸，最后泛指任何君主的宅邸。

senses.title: A bishop's residence
senses.definition: the official residence of a bishop or archbishop, often beside the cathedral
senses.definitionCN: 主教或大主教的官邸，常位于主教座堂旁
senses.example: The archbishop's palace shares a wall with the cathedral garden.
senses.exampleCN: 大主教府与主教座堂的花园共用一道墙。
senses.why: bishops held princely authority in many periods, so their houses took the same word as a king's.
senses.whyCN: 在许多时期主教握有诸侯般的权柄，因此他们的宅邸与国王用同一个词。

senses.title: A very grand private house
senses.definition: a private mansion large and ornate enough to seem royal
senses.definitionCN: 大到与华丽到看上去像王室居所的私人宅邸
senses.example: The merchant built a palace of brick beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那位商人在河边建了一座砖砌豪宅。
senses.why: wealth copies the forms of power, so a rich man's house borrows the name of a ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 财富会模仿权力的形式，因此富人的宅邸借用了君主居所的名字。

senses.title: A public palace of culture
senses.titleCN: 文化宫等大型公共建筑
senses.definition: a large state-built hall for culture, sport or exhibitions, common in former socialist countries
senses.definitionCN: 国家兴建的大型文化、体育或展览场馆，在旧社会主义国家常见
senses.example: The palace of culture has a theatre, a library and a swimming pool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座文化宫里有剧场、图书馆和游泳池。
senses.why: the state took the prestige of the palace and gave it to public leisure, so the word became civic.
senses.whyCN: 国家把宫殿的声望转给公共休闲，因此这个词变得市政化。

senses.title: Any lavish place
senses.definition: a building or room remarkable for comfort, size and expense
senses.definitionCN: 以舒适、宽敞与昂贵著称的建筑或房间
senses.example: The old cinema was a palace of red velvet and gilded plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老电影院是一座红丝绒与镀金灰泥的宫殿。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the splendour of the original, dropping the ruler entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留原义的富丽，把君主完全去掉了。

senses.title: The court as a government
senses.definition: the ruler's household and advisers, treated as a political actor
senses.definitionCN: 君主的家臣与顾问群体，被当作一个政治行为者
senses.example: The palace denied that the minister had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 王室方面否认那位大臣已被免职。
senses.why: reporters say 'the palace' when they mean the household that speaks for the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 记者说「王室」时，指的是替君主发声的那套家臣体系。

senses.title: The Palatine hill in Rome
senses.titleCN: 罗马帕拉蒂尼山上的宫殿
senses.definition: the imperial residence on the Palatine hill, whose name became the general word
senses.definitionCN: 帕拉蒂尼山上的皇帝居所，其名字成为通名
senses.example: The ruins of the palace overlook the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 宫殿废墟俯瞰着广场。
senses.why: one hill's name spread until every ruler's house in Europe carried it.
senses.whyCN: 一座山的名字扩散开来，直到欧洲每位君主的宅邸都带上了它。

senses.title: A movie palace
senses.definition: a large, lavishly decorated cinema of the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪初那种装饰华丽的大型电影院
senses.example: The movie palace seats two thousand under a painted sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电影宫在画出来的天空下可坐两千人。
senses.why: early cinemas sold an evening of luxury, so they named themselves after the most luxurious building they knew.
senses.whyCN: 早期影院卖的是一晚的奢华，因此用他们所知最奢华的建筑来命名自己。

intro.en: Palace is a place name before it is a building word: the Palatine hill in Rome gave its name to the emperor's house and then to grand houses everywhere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: palace 先是地名，后才是建筑词：罗马的帕拉蒂尼山把名字给了皇帝的宅邸，再给了各地的宏大宅邸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Palatium was the name of one of Rome's seven hills, where Augustus and later emperors built their residences.
items.cn: Palatium 是罗马七座山之一的名字，奥古斯都及后来的皇帝在此营建居所。

items.en: Because the emperor's house stood on that hill, the hill's name became a word for the house itself.
items.cn: 由于皇帝的宅邸立在那座山上，山名便成了指宅邸本身的词。

items.en: Old French palais carried the word into English, where it first named a royal residence.
items.cn: 古法语 palais 把该词带入英语，最初指王室居所。

items.en: In the Middle Ages the word widened to bishops' houses and then to any exceptionally grand town house.
items.cn: 中世纪时该词扩展到主教府，再扩展到任何格外宏大的城中宅邸。

items.en: In the twentieth century states built palaces of culture and workers' clubs, giving the word a public meaning.
items.cn: 二十世纪国家兴建文化宫与工人俱乐部，使这个词带上公共含义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of the hill name Palatium is disputed; a link to a shepherd god or to a word for a stake has been suggested, but neither is demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：山名 Palatium 的来源有争议；有人提出与牧神有关，或与表示「木桩」的词有关，但两者都未得到证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like palace or share its grand-house field but differ in origin; group two holds other grand residences.
note.cn: 第一组是与 palace 形近或同属「宏大宅邸」语义场、但来源不同的词；第二组是其他显赫居所。

entries.definition: Like a palace in size and splendour; it describes a quality and never names a building type.
entries.definitionCN: 在体量与富丽上像宫殿；描述一种性质，从不指建筑类型。

entries.definition: The domain of a count palatine, an official with royal powers in a border region; it names land and office.
entries.definitionCN: 宫廷伯爵的领地，指在边境地区拥有王权的官员辖区；指土地与职衔。

entries.definition: An Italian town house of a noble family; English borrowed it for a specific Mediterranean type.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利贵族家族的城中宅邸；英语借来表示一种特定的地中海类型。

entries.definition: A seizure of power by insiders close to the ruler; the phrase uses palace as the seat of power, not as architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 由君主身边内部人发动的夺权；短语把 palace 当作权力中心，而非建筑。

entries.definition: A fortified residence; it stresses defence, while a palace stresses display and administration.
entries.definitionCN: 设防的居所，强调防御；而 palace 强调展示与治理。

entries.definition: A very large private house; it lacks the royal or episcopal rank that palace implies.
entries.definitionCN: 极大型的私人住宅；缺少 palace 所含的王室或主教等级。

entries.definition: The neutral word for an official home, used when rank should not be emphasized.
entries.definitionCN: 指官邸的中性词，用于不宜强调等级时。

entries.definition: A French country house or estate; it combines castle and country house associations.
entries.definitionCN: 法国的乡间宅邸或庄园，兼有城堡与乡居宅邸的联想。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real hill name, the real rank words and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的山名、真实的等级词与真实的复合词。

normal.en: One hill in Rome gave its name to every royal house in Europe.
normal.cn: 罗马的一座山，把名字给了欧洲每一座王室宅邸。

normal.en: The family runs palace, palatial, palatinate, palazzo, palace coup.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 palace、palatial、palatinate、palazzo、palace coup。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: royal palace, archbishop's palace, palace of culture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：王宫、大主教府、文化宫。

normal.en: Rank decides the word: a bishop's house and a king's house can both be palaces.
normal.cn: 等级决定用词：主教的宅邸与国王的宅邸都可以叫 palace。

normal.en: The movie palace sold luxury by borrowing the most luxurious name available.
normal.cn: 电影宫借用了当时最奢华的名字来售卖奢华。

abstract.en: Picture a house that has swallowed a whole hill and now wears its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子吞下了整座山，并把山名穿在身上。

abstract.en: Picture a private hallway so long that a guest needs a map to reach the dining room.
abstract.cn: 想象一条私家长廊，长到客人要拿地图才找得到餐厅。

abstract.en: Picture a cinema whose ceiling is painted as a night sky, so the audience sits outdoors indoors.
abstract.cn: 想象一座影院把天花板画成夜空，观众于是在室内坐在户外。

examples.en: The palace was opened as a museum after the monarchy ended.
examples.cn: 君主制结束后，这座王宫被改为博物馆开放。

examples.en: The archbishop's palace dates from the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 大主教府始建于十二世纪。

examples.en: They restored the movie palace instead of demolishing it.
examples.cn: 他们修复了那座电影宫，而没有将其拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: Palatium（罗马帕拉蒂尼山）→ 山上皇帝宅邸 → 宫殿、豪华宅邸

root: 拉丁 Palatium 原为罗马七丘之一的名字，因皇帝宅邸建于其上而转指宫殿；经古法语 palais 入英语。山名本身的来源不确定。英语 palace。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one address: a ruler's house on a hill becomes a bishop's house, a rich man's house, a public hall, a metaphor, a government, a ruin and a cinema.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个住处展开：山上的君主宅邸成为主教府、富商大宅、公共厅堂、比喻、政府、废墟与影院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gate, courtyard, stair and inner hall, each layer admitting fewer people than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：门、院、阶、内殿，每一层允许进入的人都比前一层更少。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL HOUSE: the hill name became the emperor's residence, and that residence became the general word.
branches.cn: 最初的宅邸：山名成为皇帝居所之名，那座居所又成为通名。

branches.en: PRINCELY CLERGY: a bishop's house takes the royal word because bishops held princely power.
branches.cn: 诸侯般的主教：主教府沿用王室用词，因为主教握有诸侯般的权力。

branches.en: WEALTH COPIES POWER: a merchant's mansion and a lavish hotel borrow palace's splendour without a ruler.
branches.cn: 财富模仿权力：富商豪宅与豪华旅馆借走了 palace 的富丽，却不要君主。

branches.en: PUBLIC SPLENDOUR: the state builds palaces of culture, and cinemas call themselves movie palaces.
branches.cn: 公共的富丽：国家兴建文化宫，影院则自称电影宫。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the building's name moves to the people who speak for the ruler.
branches.cn: 家臣体系：建筑之名转到替君主发声的那群人身上。

intro.en: Palace has no prefix or suffix of its own: it is a place name that became a noun, and its derived words are built on that noun.
intro.cn: palace 本身没有前缀或后缀：它是一个变成名词的地名，其派生词都建在这个名词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin Palatium supplied the name, and the adjective palatinus described what belonged to the imperial hill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Palatium 提供了这个名字，形容词 palatinus 描述属于皇帝那座山的事物。

items.structure: Palatium (Latin proper noun, the Palatine hill)
items.example: Palatium named a place before it named a building.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字先指地点，后指建筑。

items.meaning: of the Palatine; of the imperial court
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述一位宫廷官员。

items.example: Old French carried the hill's name to a house.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把山名带到了房子上。

items.example: The flat has a palatial bathroom.
items.exampleCN: 这套公寓有一间宫殿般的浴室。

items.meaning: the territory of a count palatine
items.example: The palatinate had its own courts.
The palazzo opens onto a small square.
items.exampleCN: 这座府邸朝向一个小广场。

items.meaning: a seizure of power from inside the court
items.meaningCN: 由宫廷内部发动的夺权
items.example: A palace coup removed the old guard.
items.exampleCN: 一场宫廷政变清除了旧班底。

latinEntries.meaning: the Palatine hill; the imperial residence
of the Palatine or the court

definition_zh: 进入；参加；报名参加；输入（数据）；走进
definition_en: to go or come into a place; to take part in; to put information into a system
core_image: 跨过门槛：从外面一步走进里面
scene: 校门口闸机打开，学生刷卡走进考场。 The students entered the exam room one by one.
sceneCN: 这里 enter 是「进入」（第 1 个义项：走进一个地方）；句意是学生们依次进入考场。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ance 后缀构成，义为「入口；进入」
同根变体名词，义为「进入；条目；参赛作品」
同根加前缀的名词，义为「娱乐；款待」

senses.title: To go or come into a place
senses.definition: to move from outside into a room, building or area
senses.definitionCN: 从外面走进房间、建筑或某个区域
senses.example: Please knock before you enter the office.
senses.exampleCN: 进办公室前请先敲门。
senses.why: The Latin root means to step across, so the image is one foot crossing the threshold.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根意为「跨步」，画面是一只脚跨过门槛。

senses.title: To take part in or join
senses.definition: to become a participant in a competition, exam or organization
senses.definitionCN: 成为比赛、考试或组织的参与者
senses.example: She decided to enter the speech contest.
senses.exampleCN: 她决定参加演讲比赛。
senses.why: Joining a contest is stepping into a field of players, an extension of crossing into a space.
senses.whyCN: 参加比赛就像走进选手的场地，是「跨入空间」意象的延伸。

senses.title: To put information into a system
senses.definition: to record information in a book, list or computer system
senses.definitionCN: 把信息记录在册、清单或电脑系统中
senses.example: Enter your password and press the button.
senses.exampleCN: 输入密码然后按下按钮。
senses.why: Data is made to go inside a machine, the same crossing image moved to paper and screens.
senses.whyCN: 数据被送进机器，同样的跨入画面移动到纸张与屏幕上。

senses.title: To become a member of a group or stage
senses.definition: to begin to belong to a profession, school or period of life
senses.definitionCN: 开始属于某个职业、学校或人生阶段
senses.example: He entered politics at a young age.
senses.exampleCN: 他很年轻就步入政界。
senses.why: A new stage of life is a new room, so joining it reuses the doorway picture.
senses.whyCN: 人生新阶段是一间新房间，加入它就复用门廊的画面。

intro.en: Enter comes from Old French entrer, from Latin intrare, built on intra meaning 'inside'. The core has always been crossing a line into a space.
intro.cn: enter 经古法语 entrer，来自拉丁语 intrare，词基 intra 意为「在内」。核心始终是跨过界线进入空间。

items.en: Latin intra meant 'inside, within', the root idea of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 intra 意为「在内、在内侧」，是整个词族的根意。

items.en: The verb intrare meant 'to go into, to enter', used of walking in as well as beginning something.
items.cn: 动词 intrare 意为「走进、进入」，既指走进，也指开始某事。

items.en: Old French entrer carried the verb into medieval European speech, still meaning to go in.
items.cn: 古法语 entrer 把动词带进中世纪欧洲语言，仍指进入。

items.en: English borrowed enter in the fourteenth century for both physical entry and joining activities.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 enter，兼指实际进入与参加活动。

items.en: Computing added the data sense and the Enter key, extending the crossing image to screens.
items.cn: 计算领域增加了输入数据义与回车键，把跨入画面延伸到屏幕上。

note.en: The first group collects the same Latin intra family; the second collects near meanings about going in or joining.
note.cn: 第一组收集同一拉丁词 intra 的词族；第二组收集与「进入、参加」相关的近义词。

entries.definition: the door or gate by which one enters, or the act of entering
entries.definitionCN: 入口；进入。由 enter 加 -ance 构成。

entries.definition: the act of entering, an item in a list, or a contest submission
entries.definitionCN: 进入；条目；参赛作品。与 enter 同根的变体名词。

entries.definition: whole, unbroken; from the same Latin idea of what is held inside
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；同源于「包含在内」的拉丁语概念，词义已偏移。

senses.why: When light leaves, seeing fails, and the state takes a name of its own.

senses.title: Deep in colour

senses.example: He chose a dark green school bag.
senses.exampleCN: 他选了一个深绿色的书包。
senses.why: Colours that drink more light sit near black, so deep shades share the word.

senses.title: The time when the sun is down
senses.definition: the hours without daylight, or the moment night begins

senses.example: We must return home before dark in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天我们必须在天黑前回家。
senses.why: Light sets the clock of the day; when it ends, the darkness is the time itself.
senses.whyCN: 日光划定一天的时钟；日光结束时，黑暗便成了那段时间本身。

items.en: The noun use grew: the dark meant the hours without sun.

items.en: The colour sense spread from shadows to clothes and paints.

definition_en: telling the truth and not cheating or stealing; showing sincerity
core_image: 摊开的手心：把知道的全部给你看，一点不藏
scene: 钱包躺在路边，他捡起后立刻交给了老师，没有打开看。 He is honest: he returned the wallet without even opening it.
sceneCN: 这里 honest 是「诚实的」（第 1 个义项：不说谎、不贪心）；他捡到钱包原样归还，连看都没看。

senses.title: Telling the truth
senses.definition: someone who is honest tells the truth and does not lie or cheat
senses.definitionCN: 说真话、不撒谎、不作弊的人
senses.example: An honest student wrote her own name on the list of wrong answers.
senses.exampleCN: 一名诚实的学生在错题名单上写下了自己的名字。
senses.why: The open hand is the picture: everything is shown, nothing hidden.
senses.whyCN: 意象是摊开的手心：全都亮给你看，毫无隐藏。

senses.title: Not stealing or cheating
senses.definition: not taking things that belong to others and not cheating in games or business
senses.definitionCN: 不拿别人的东西，不做游戏或生意中的手脚
senses.example: The honest shopkeeper gave back the extra change.
senses.exampleCN: 那位正直的店主退回了多找的零钱。
senses.why: Honesty keeps its hands still: what is not yours stays where it is.
senses.whyCN: 诚实的手不乱动：不属于你的东西就留在原处。

senses.title: Sincere and direct
senses.definition: showing real feelings and saying directly what you think
senses.definitionCN: 流露真实感受，直接说出想法
senses.example: To be honest, I did not like the film very much.
senses.exampleCN: 说实话，我不太喜欢那部电影。
senses.why: An honest word may be hard to hear, but it is given with an open heart.
senses.whyCN: 坦诚的话可能不好听，但出自一颗敞开的心。

intro.en: Honest came through Old French from Latin honestus, meaning honoured or respectable, from honos, honour.
intro.cn: honest 经古法语来自拉丁 honestus「受尊敬的、体面的」，其词根是 honos（荣誉）。

items.en: Latin honos meant honour and public respect; its adjective honestus meant respectable.
items.cn: 拉丁 honos 指荣誉与公众尊重，其形容词 honestus 意为体面的。

items.en: Old French honeste and oneste carried the word into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 honeste、oneste 把这个词带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English borrowed honest around the thirteenth century, first meaning respectable.
items.cn: 中古英语约在十三世纪借入 honest，最初意为可敬的。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the sense to truthful and sincere.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义收窄为诚实的、真诚的。

items.en: The letter h is not pronounced: honest sounds like on-ist, so we say an honest person.
items.cn: h 不发音：honest 读作 on-ist，因此冠词用 an honest person。

note.en: Group one holds the silent-h family; group two holds words for truthfulness and fairness.
note.cn: 第一组是 h 不发音的词族；第二组是表示真实与公正的近义词。

normal.cn: honest、honour、hour 三个词的 h 都不发音，一起记。

normal.en: to be honest is a polite way to start a true opinion

normal.en: honest work means work earned by real effort
normal.cn: honest work 指凭真本事挣来的正当工作。

abstract.cn: 想象两只摊开的手掌，空无一物——没藏任何东西。

abstract.en: Picture a shopkeeper sliding back one extra coin across the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象店主把一枚多找的硬币推回柜台对面。

abstract.en: Feel the weight lift when the truth is finally spoken.
abstract.cn: 感受真话终于说出口后心里变轻的那一瞬。

examples.en: The honest taxi driver returned the phone to the station.
examples.cn: 诚实的出租车司机把手机送回了车站。

examples.en: To be honest, the soup needs a little more salt.
examples.cn: 说实话，这汤还差点盐。

examples.en: A game is fun only when everyone plays honest.
examples.cn: 只有大家都守规矩，游戏才好玩。

definition_zh: 属于；应放在（某处）；是……的成员；适合
definition_en: to be owned by someone, to be a member of a group, or to be in the right place
core_image: 每件物品上都贴着写有主人名字的标签
scene: 教室的失物招领架上，放着一堆没人认领的文具。 The blue scarf belongs to my sister.
sceneCN: 这里 belong 是「属于」（第 1 个义项：所有权归某人）；句意为这条蓝围巾属于我姐姐。

pos.zh: 动词：属于；应放在；是成员；适合

collocations.zh: 属于这里；本来就该在这儿

derivatives.zh: 由 belong 加 -ing 构成，义为「归属感；所有物」
belonging 的复数，义为「随身财物；所有物」

senses.title: To be owned by someone
senses.definition: for an object to be the property of a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 指某件物品是某个人的财产
senses.example: The blue scarf belongs to my sister.
senses.exampleCN: 这条蓝围巾属于我姐姐。
senses.why: Old English gelang meant pertaining or dependent, and belong joined it with be-, so the word first says that a thing hangs on or attaches to an owner.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gelang 意为「属于、依附于」，belong 让它与 be- 结合，所以这个词最初表示某物挂在或附在某个主人身上。

senses.title: To be in the right place
senses.definition: for an object to have a proper or usual place
senses.definitionCN: 指某件物品有它该在或通常所在的位置
senses.example: This chair belongs in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子应该放在角落里。
senses.why: If a thing attaches to its owner, it can also attach to a place, so the ownership sense gives the sense of the spot where a thing properly stays.
senses.whyCN: 既然东西会附在主人身上，它也会附在某个位置上，于是所有权义给出了「某物本该待在哪里」的义项。

senses.title: To be a member of a group
senses.definition: for a person to be a member of a group, club, family, or team
senses.definitionCN: 指某人是某个团体、俱乐部、家庭或球队的成员
senses.example: She belongs to the school choir.
senses.exampleCN: 她是学校合唱团的成员。
senses.why: Attaching is the same picture for people: a person attaches to a group and becomes one of its members.
senses.whyCN: 「附着」用在人身上是同一幅画：一个人附在一个团体上，就成了它的一员。

senses.title: To suit each other
senses.definition: for two people or things to be right together
senses.definitionCN: 指两个人或两样东西放在一起很合适
senses.example: You and I belong together.
senses.exampleCN: 你和我很相配。
senses.why: When two things each attach to the other, neither is out of place, and that picture is exactly the sense of belonging together.
senses.whyCN: 当两样东西彼此附着，谁都不显得别扭，这幅画正是 belong together「相配」的意思。

intro.en: Belong began as a compound meaning to pertain, and it later spread to ownership and membership.
intro.cn: belong 最初是意为「属于、相关」的复合词，后来扩展到所有权与成员身份。

items.en: Old English gelang meant belonging to or dependent on something.
items.cn: 古英语 gelang 意为「属于某物、依附于某物」。

items.en: Middle English joined be- with a verb from this root, giving belongen, to pertain or to be fitting.
items.cn: 中古英语把 be- 与来自这个词根的动词结合，形成 belongen，意为「相关、合适」。

items.en: The prefix added the idea of being attached around something.
items.cn: 这个前缀增添了「环绕着某物附着」的意思。

items.en: From ownership the verb spread to the right place of an object, membership in a group, and suitability between people.
items.cn: 从所有权出发，这个动词扩展到物体的正确位置、团体中的成员身份，以及人与人之间的合适。

items.en: Today belong almost always appears with to or with a place phrase, and belonging also names a sense of attachment.

normal.cn: 古英语 gelang 表示「属于、相关」，be- 增添「附着」的意思，所以 belong 就是附在某个主人身上。

normal.en: The same picture covers a group: a person attaches to a team and becomes a member.
normal.cn: 同一幅画也覆盖团体：一个人附在球队上，就成了它的成员。

normal.en: Belonging is the noun for attachment, and belongings are the things you carry.
normal.cn: belonging 是表示「归属」的名词，belongings 则是随身带的财物。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with to, here, together and in.
normal.cn: 它常与 to、here、together、in 搭配。

abstract.en: Move the tag from an owner to a shelf and then to a choir: ownership, place and membership share one tag.
abstract.cn: 把标签从主人移到架子，再移到合唱团：所有权、位置和成员身份共用一张标签。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the name tag bring the meaning back.

examples.en: She belongs to the school choir.

root: belong 来自中古英语 belongen，源于古英语 gelang「属于、依附」，并由 be- 增添「附着于」的意思。它最初表示「与某物相关」，随后从所有权扩展到物体的正确位置、团体中的成员身份，以及人与人之间的相配关系。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of belong come from one picture: something attached to something else, whether to an owner, a place, a group, or another thing.
sensesIntro.cn: belong 的四个义项都出自同一幅画面：一物附着在另一物上，无论附着的是主人、位置、团体，还是另一个东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name tag on every object in a lost-property shelf
core.cn: 核心意象：失物招领架上每件物品都贴着名字标签

branches.cn: 主人线：附在一个人身上，就形成「财产」义。

branches.cn: 位置线：附在一个位置上，就形成「应放在此处」义。

branches.cn: 团体线：附在一个团体上，就形成「成员身份」义。

branches.cn: 配合线：两样东西彼此附着，就形成「相配」义。

branches.en: THE ONE PICTURE: property and membership are both attachments, one to a person and one to a group.
branches.cn: 同一幅画：所有权与成员身份都是「附着」，一个附在个人，一个附在团体。

definition_zh: 方向；方位；指导；指挥；（电影的）导演
definition_en: the way something faces or moves; instructions or guidance
core_image: 一支箭头指向一条路的走向
scene: 在操场集合时，老师喊口令。 Turn left, then walk in the direction of the school gate.
sceneCN: 这里 direction 是「方向」（第 1 个义项：朝向哪里）；句意是向左转，然后朝校门的方向走。

derivatives.zh: direction 的动词与形容词形式，义为「直接的；指挥」
direction 加后缀变化构成，义为「导演；主管」
direct 加 -ly 构成，义为「直接地」

senses.title: The way something faces or moves
senses.definition: the line or course along which someone or something moves or faces
senses.definitionCN: 人或物移动、朝向的路线
senses.example: The birds flew off in the direction of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟群朝湖的方向飞去了。
senses.why: Directus means laid straight, and direction names the line a thing lies along.
senses.whyCN: directus 意为「排成直线」，direction 便指事物所沿的那条线。

senses.title: Instructions or guidance
senses.definition: orders or advice about what to do
senses.definitionCN: 关于做什么的命令或建议
senses.example: Follow the directions on the box before you take the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 吃药前先按照盒子上的说明来。
senses.why: A straight line has one clear way, so telling people the way became giving directions.
senses.whyCN: 直线只有一条清晰的路，指明这条路便成了「下指示」。

senses.title: Control of a performance or activity
senses.definition: the act of deciding how a film, play or team is run
senses.definitionCN: 决定电影、戏剧或队伍如何进行的举动
senses.example: The direction of the school play was excellent this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年校剧的导演工作非常出色。
senses.why: When someone keeps a group moving straight toward its goal, that steering is called direction.
senses.whyCN: 当有人带领集体径直走向目标时，这种引领就被称作 direction。

intro.en: Direction is the noun form of the Latin make-straight family.
intro.cn: direction 是拉丁语「拉直」词族的名词形式。

items.en: Latin dirigere meant to lay straight, from di- (apart) and regere (to make straight, to rule).
items.cn: 拉丁语 dirigere 意为使成直线，由 di-（分开）加 regere（使直、统治）构成。

items.en: The past participle directus meant straight.
items.cn: 过去分词 directus 意为直的。

items.en: Late Latin formed directio, the act of laying straight.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语派生出 directio，指拉直这一行为。

items.en: Old French carried direcion into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语以 direcion 将其带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: English took direction in the fourteenth century, first for roads and lines.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 direction，最早用于道路与直线。

items.en: Later senses grew: orders, steering a team, and directing films.
items.cn: 后来长出指示、指挥团队、导演电影等义项。

note.en: These words share the regere root or the way-finding field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 regere 词根，或属于找路义场。

normalIntro.cn: 用「箭头」画面和 rect- 词族来记。

normal.en: follow the directions on the medicine box.

abstract.en: Picture an arrow pinned on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉在地图上的箭头。

abstract.en: Feel the compass needle settle toward north.
abstract.cn: 体会指南针稳稳指向北方的感觉。

abstract.en: Hear a coach shouting left or right.
abstract.cn: 听教练喊着左、右的口令。

examples.en: When the bell rang, students ran in all directions.
examples.cn: 铃一响，学生们向四面八方跑去。

examples.en: Read the directions carefully before you start the experiment.
examples.cn: 开始实验前请仔细阅读操作说明。

examples.en: Her hard work gave the club a new direction.
examples.cn: 她的努力让俱乐部有了新的方向。

definition_zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的
definition_en: existing in nature rather than made by people; also inborn, and normal or expected
core_image: 一株野草从石缝里自己钻出来，没有人去栽种
scene: 山脚下有一片从未开垦的林地，藤蔓顺着倒下的树干自己爬上去。 The reserve protects the natural habitat of the local birds.
sceneCN: 这里 natural 是「自然的、天然的」（第 1 个义项：非人造）；句意为保护区守护当地鸟类的天然栖息地。图中可辨识物件：倒木、藤蔓、林地。

pos.zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的

derivatives.zh: 由 natural 加 -ly 构成，义为「自然地；当然」
由 natural 加 -ness 构成，义为「自然；不做作」
由 natural 加 -ist 构成，义为「博物学家」
由 natural 加 -ize 构成，义为「使入籍；使自然化」

senses.title: Existing in nature, not made by people
senses.definition: found in nature and produced without human making or control
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、并非由人制造或控制而产生的
senses.example: The park protects the natural habitat of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着鸟类的天然栖息地。
senses.why: The Latin noun natura names the way things are born and grow, so natural starts from what comes into being without human hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 natura 指事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 的起点是未经人手而生成的东西。

senses.title: Inborn rather than learned
senses.definition: present in a person or animal from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 人与生俱来、并非后天学到的
senses.example: She has a natural gift for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生就有语言天赋。
senses.why: If natura is the way something is born, a quality that arrives at birth is literally natural, which is why talent can be natural.
senses.whyCN: 既然 natura 指事物出生时的样子，出生就带来的特质自然就是「天生的」，天赋也就能说成 natural。

senses.title: Normal and to be expected
senses.definition: what normally happens and therefore does not surprise anyone
senses.definitionCN: 按常理会发生，因此不令人意外
senses.example: It is natural to feel nervous before a test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前感到紧张是正常的。
senses.why: What follows nature follows a regular course, so natural extends from how things grow to how things usually happen.
senses.whyCN: 顺着本性发展的东西有其常规，于是 natural 从「事物如何生长」扩展到「事情通常如何发生」。

senses.title: Relaxed and not put on
senses.definition: used of behaviour or manner that is easy and sincere, with no pretending
senses.definitionCN: 形容举止轻松真诚，不装样子
senses.example: His smile was warm and natural.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑容温暖而自然。
senses.why: A person who behaves as nature made them, without forcing a pose, looks natural, which gives the word its social sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个人按本性行事、不硬摆姿势，看上去就是 natural，这就是这个词的社交义。

intro.en: Natural comes from the Latin noun natura, which itself grows out of nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: natural 来自拉丁名词 natura，而 natura 又由 nasci（出生）生长出来。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born, the root behind nature, native and innate.
items.cn: nasci 意为出生，是 nature、native、innate 共同的根。

items.en: Natura named the character or course of things, what a thing is born to be.
items.cn: natura 指事物的本性或进程，即事物生来就该有的样子。

items.en: Naturalis meant belonging to nature or coming from birth.
items.cn: naturalis 意为属于自然的，或与生俱来的。

items.en: Old French naturel passed into Middle English natural, keeping both the world sense and the inborn sense.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 进入中古英语作 natural，同时保留「自然界」和「天生」两义。

items.en: Modern English adds the meanings normal and unaffected, which grow from the idea of following nature.
items.cn: 现代英语又添「正常」与「不做作」两义，都由「顺其自然」的想法长出。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same birth stem; the near-meaning group collects words for what is normal and inborn.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「出生」词干上的词；近义组收表示正常与天生的词。

entries.definition: The physical world and the character built into a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 物质世界，以及事物内在的本性。

entries.definition: Born in a particular place, or belonging there by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 在某个地方出生的；原产的。

entries.definition: Present in a person from birth, not learned.
entries.definitionCN: 人与生俱来的，并非学来的。

entries.definition: What is usual and expected, with nothing odd about it.
entries.definitionCN: 通常而合乎预期的，没有异常之处。

entries.definition: Existing in a person from birth rather than gained later.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来而非后天获得的。

entries.definition: Grown or produced without artificial chemicals or processes.
entries.definitionCN: 不使用人工化学物或工艺而生长、生产的。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun of birth and three English endings that build an adverb, a noun and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「出生」的拉丁名词和三个英语词尾支撑，分别构成副词、名词和动词。

normal.en: Natura is Latin for the way things are born and grow, so natural is first about the world, not about people.
normal.cn: natura 是拉丁语中事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 首先说的是世界，而不是人。

normal.en: Naturally adds -ly, and it doubles as an answer word meaning of course.
normal.cn: naturally 加 -ly 构成，它还有一个「当然」的用法。

normal.en: Native and innate share the same birth root, one meaning born in a place, the other born in a person.
normal.cn: native 与 innate 共用同一个「出生」的词根，一个指在某地出生，一个指天生。

normal.en: Natural gas and natural resources are fixed phrases, so natural here means unprocessed, not easy.
normal.cn: natural gas 与 natural resources 是固定搭配，这里的 natural 指未经加工，而不是轻松。

normal.en: A natural death means death by age or illness, not by accident or violence.
normal.cn: natural death 指因年老或疾病死亡，而不是意外或暴力致死。

abstract.en: A word that begins with the world and ends with good manners shows how deeply English ties sincerity to nature.
abstract.cn: 一个词从自然界开始、到得体举止结束，说明英语把「真诚」紧紧系在「自然」上。

abstract.en: Calling something natural is often a quiet claim that nothing has been added to it.
abstract.cn: 说某物是 natural，常常是在悄悄声明没有往里面添加别的东西。

abstract.en: When a gift is called natural, praise and modesty arrive in the same word.
abstract.cn: 当一份天赋被叫作 natural，赞美与谦逊同时落在同一个词里。

examples.en: This valley is one of the few natural habitats left for the species.
examples.cn: 这条山谷是该物种仅存的几处天然栖息地之一。

examples.en: He has a natural ability to make strangers feel at ease.
examples.cn: 他天生就有让陌生人放松的本事。

examples.en: It is natural to miss home during the first month abroad.
examples.cn: 出国头一个月想家是正常的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈求若」——真正的自然不必强求，顺其自然就会来；记住 natural 是自然的。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is what nature produces; from it the word reaches inborn qualities, expected behaviour and social ease.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是自然界生成的东西；由此延伸到天生的特质、合乎常理的行为以及举止自然。

branches.cn: 一百年没人打扰的林地

branches.cn: 嗓音仿佛无需训练的歌者

branches.cn: 没准备笑话却笑出声的主人

senses.title: A sickness or disease
senses.definition: a condition of bad health; a disease
senses.definitionCN: 健康状况不佳的状态；疾病
senses.example: He caught an illness on the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 他在船上得了病。
senses.why: The name covers any state of being unwell, from colds to worse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词涵盖任何不健康的状态，从感冒到更重的病。

senses.title: The period of being ill
senses.definition: the time during which someone is ill

intro.en: Illness is ill plus -ness, the state suffix. The pair fixed itself in English in the fifteenth century as ill, borrowed from Old Norse, spread south.
intro.cn: illness 由 ill 加状态后缀 -ness 构成。十五世纪，随着诺斯语借词 ill 向南传播，这一组合在英语中定型。

items.en: The base ill comes from Old Norse illr, bad.
items.cn: 词基 ill 来自古诺斯语 illr「坏」。

items.en: Middle English added the suffix -nesse to ill, first meaning badness in general.
items.cn: 中古英语给 ill 加后缀 -nesse，最初泛指恶劣。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the word leaned toward sickness and poor health.
items.cn: 至十五世纪，词义偏向疾病与不健康。

items.en: Modern English separated illness from disease: illness is the patient's state, disease the named condition.
items.cn: 现代英语将 illness 与 disease 分开：illness 指病人的状态，disease 指有名称的病症。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries added mental illness and public-health usage.
items.cn: 十九二十世纪加入 mental illness 与公共卫生用法。

note.en: The look-alike group lists sickness nouns. The meaning group separates the patient's state from the named disease.
note.cn: 形近组列出疾病类名词；词义组区分病人状态与病名。

items.en: Modern English fixed eighteenth as the regular ordinal of eighteen.
